_about: Caricature traditions, tiered for a kind channel. A = house styles, B = with care, C = history only, exclude = never.

traditions.name: Classic newspaper editorial cartoon
traditions.era: 1940s to now; US, UK, Canada, Australia [GK]
traditions.visual_dna: one panel, one idea, a caption or speech balloon, labelled symbols, dramatic staging of a single "act"
traditions.linework: brush or nib ink with confident thick-to-thin strokes
traditions.palette: black ink plus grey wash, or limited flat colour (muted reds, blues, ochre)
traditions.background: minimal props, a horizon line or a sketched setting (podium, desk, TV studio)
traditions.lighting: flat, with tone from wash rather than a light source
traditions.best_use: the channel's **default "verdict" frame**: seller holding the false claim, with a fact card beside
prompt_elements: bold brush-ink outlines with thick-to-thin strokes
simplified gesture body, oversized expressive head
sparse sketched background with horizon line
clear silhouette, readable at small size

traditions.name: Urbane magazine editorial illustration
traditions.visual_dna: elegant, economical line, dry wit, lots of air, and soft watercolour or gouache washes that don't fill the lines exactly
traditions.linework: thin, varied nib or pencil line, sometimes broken or wobbly
traditions.palette: muted washes (sage, dusty blue, warm grey, pale ochre) on cream paper
traditions.background: interiors suggested in a few lines (sofa, window, cocktail party)
traditions.lighting: soft and ambient, from the wash alone
traditions.best_use: **the most on-brand "calm, kind" look.** Good for explainers and the narrator's world, and for showing sellers without venom
prompt_elements: loose watercolour wash slightly off the lines
muted sage, dusty blue and warm grey palette
minimal interior suggested in a few lines

traditions.name: 18th-century British hand-coloured etching
traditions.visual_dna: etched line with hatching, hand-tinted watercolour, crowded stage-like compositions, long captions, speech written in looping balloons [GK for the balloons]
traditions.face_body: extreme grotesque, including bloated or emaciated bodies, bulging eyes and huge chins
traditions.linework: fine etched lines, parallel hatching and crosshatching, stipple
traditions.palette: transparent hand-tint washes (rose, Prussian blue, yellow ochre, green) on off-white laid paper
traditions.lighting: none modelled, apart from etched shadow hatching
traditions.best_use: **historical-flashback segments** ("people have sold miracle cures for centuries")
traditions.tone_risk: **high if used on modern people.** The tradition is scatological and grotesque about bodies
prompt_elements: transparent watercolour hand-tinting in rose, blue and ochre
off-white laid paper with plate mark

traditions.name: 19th-century French lithographic caricature
traditions.visual_dna: soft crayon lithograph tone, sculptural heads, sombre human observation
traditions.face_body: big heads about 1/3 of height in the portrait-bust caricatures [GK]
traditions.linework: greasy crayon strokes, scribbled tonal shading, soft edges
traditions.background: courtrooms, salons, streets, rendered as loose tone
traditions.motion: slow camera moves over a still frame; a subtle head turn; crayon "boil" (frame-to-frame line jitter)
traditions.lighting: chiaroscuro, with strong side light modelled in crayon
traditions.best_use: **serious-tone segments about systems** (paid promotion, grift economics)
prompt_elements: sculptural oversized head with heavy jowls
black and grey on cream paper

traditions.name: Modern crude-line French satirical weekly look
traditions.visual_dna: deliberately crude, fast felt-pen line, flat garish colour, shock humour
traditions.face_body: big nose, wild eyes, spaghetti limbs, deliberately ugly
traditions.tone_risk: **very high.** The style is built on offence, including religious offence

traditions.name: Late-19th-century American political cartoon
traditions.visual_dna: dense wood-engraved line, allegorical figures (a star-spangled national uncle, a classical lady personifying the nation, party animals, a tiger for a political machine), labelled objects, big crowd or panorama scenes
traditions.face_body: near-realistic bodies with exaggerated heads (head about 1/4 of height)
traditions.linework: engraved parallel lines, heavy crosshatching, a strong black mass
traditions.best_use: **history/B-roll and "symbol" scenes.** The animal-as-party convention is usable but risks reading as partisan
prompt_elements: dense parallel engraved lines and crosshatching
allegorical scene with labelled props (blank labels)
exaggerated bearded head on realistic body
top hat, waistcoat and watch chain

traditions.name: Early-20th-century German satirical weekly poster style
traditions.visual_dna: bold flat colour shapes, clean ink contour, poster-like silhouettes, Art Nouveau-era design sense, a mascot animal as symbol (a red bulldog for the people) [Jugendstil link is GK; the source did not mention it]
traditions.linework: clean, even-weight ink contour, sometimes a loose pen line (Kley)
traditions.palette: 2–4 flat spot colours (brick red, mustard, olive, black) on cream
traditions.background: flat colour field or a minimal stage
traditions.motion: **very good for animation.** Flat shapes work for vector-style rigging and graphic transitions
traditions.best_use: **title cards, chapter openers, "pattern of the grift" diagrams.** Its graphic boldness is stylish without cruelty
prompt_elements: bold flat spot colours brick red, mustard and black

traditions.name: British latex-puppet satire as a 2D drawing
traditions.visual_dna: sculpted, rubbery, glossy skin; hugely enlarged heads; one signature prop or colour gimmick per character (cigar, grey skin, gin bottle)
traditions.palette: fleshy pinks and saturated wardrobe colours on a TV-studio set
traditions.motion: puppet-like mouth flaps and jerky arm movement
traditions.lighting: hard studio key light with glossy latex highlights
traditions.best_use: the **"signature prop" idea** is excellent for the owner's design record (e.g
traditions.tone_risk: **high.** It is built on making people look physically repulsive
prompt_elements: glossy rubbery skin with specular highlights
oversized head on small puppet body

traditions.name: Celebrity / theatre line caricature
traditions.visual_dna: one flowing calligraphic line, rhythmic swirls for hair and costume, the character captured mid-performance, lots of white page
traditions.linework: continuous swelling and tapering pen or brush line, no hatching, black on white
traditions.background: none, or a stage edge and a spotlight pool
traditions.motion: **excellent.** Line-draw-on animation (the stroke writes itself), elegant gestural motion
traditions.best_use: **affectionate, classy portraits.** Good for introducing a person neutrally before the fact-check, and for the mascot cast
traditions.tone_risk: **very low.** It is a celebrating tradition, not an attacking one
prompt_elements: rhythmic swirling lines for hair and fabric

traditions.name: Theme-park live caricature
traditions.era: 1970s–now, US theme parks and fairs (Tom Richmond)
traditions.visual_dna: huge head on a tiny "body gag" doing a hobby (surfing, golfing), bright airbrushed or marker colour, smiling and flattering exaggeration
traditions.linework: confident marker or graphite outline on the face, simple body
traditions.palette: bright airbrush gradients (sky blue, sunset orange) and skin highlights
traditions.background: an airbrushed gradient or a simple prop scene
traditions.lighting: soft airbrushed highlights on the forehead and cheeks
traditions.best_use: **friendly, upbeat moments.** The "body gag" format is perfect for "seller doing the documented act" (counting cash, holding a supplement bottle)
prompt_elements: live caricature, giant head on tiny body
tiny cartoon body doing an activity

traditions.name: Comic-convention digital caricature
traditions.visual_dna: polished digital painting, dramatic exaggeration, pop-culture costume, painterly rendering with rim light
traditions.linework: little or no line; painted forms
traditions.background: a dramatic gradient, an energy burst, or a genre backdrop
traditions.motion: 2.5D parallax, camera push, hair and cape physics

traditions.name: Painted magazine-cover caricature
traditions.visual_dna: hyper-detailed gouache or acrylic painting, realistic rendering of absurd exaggeration, glossy, centred subject with a gag prop
traditions.face_body: big head (1/3 to 1/2 of height), every pore rendered
traditions.palette: rich saturated paint, warm skin tones, bold flat backgrounds behind the cover figure
traditions.background: a flat colour field or a vignette
traditions.lighting: classic portrait lighting with a glossy highlight
prompt_elements: centred subject holding a gag prop

traditions.name: Children's-book characterisation
traditions.visual_dna: soft rounded shapes, warm textures (gouache, coloured pencil, watercolour), kindly faces
traditions.linework: soft pencil or textured brush, sometimes no outline
traditions.best_use: **the narrator/mascot world and believer-sympathetic scenes** ("people trusted this because...")

traditions.name: Newspaper comic-strip character design
traditions.visual_dna: highly simplified, iconic, repeatable characters with a strong silhouette, read in 3–4 panels, clean even line, flat colour
traditions.palette: flat primaries or limited Sunday-strip colours
traditions.motion: **excellent and cheap.** Consistent model sheets make AI character consistency easier
traditions.best_use: **recurring segments, the mascot, and quick "panel gag" summaries.** Very kind tone
prompt_elements: simplified iconic face with dot eyes

traditions.name: Japanese exaggeration: manga reaction faces, chibi / super-deformed
traditions.visual_dna: SD bodies with heads 1/3 to 1/2 of height, big eyes, stubby limbs
traditions.background: speed lines, screentone patterns, sparkles, or plain colour
prompt_elements: super-deformed chibi proportions, head one third of body

traditions.name: Mexican political cartoon / relief-print calavera
traditions.visual_dna: relief-print or engraved black line, distressed ink, skeleton figures in fashionable clothes, broadside layout with verse
traditions.face_body: skeletons, or caricatures with big heads on engraved bodies
traditions.linework: gouged relief line, heavy black, rough ink texture
traditions.palette: black on coloured broadside paper (pink, yellow, green) [paper colours GK]
traditions.motion: cut-out skeleton puppets, a print "stamp" reveal
traditions.best_use: possibly the **"old scam, new face" history segments.**
traditions.tone_risk: **medium to high.** Skeleton imagery used on a living person can read as a death wish
prompt_elements: caricature with big head on engraved body

traditions.name: Soviet satirical magazine style
traditions.visual_dna: confident brush caricature, flat poster colour, heroic "people" against tiny, grotesque enemies (capitalists in top hats, fascists), propaganda clarity
traditions.face_body: enemies are shrunken, bloated or animalised
traditions.linework: fluid brush ink with watercolour or gouache fills
traditions.palette: red, black, ochre and cream; some saturated covers
traditions.best_use: **only as a historical example of propaganda** (good for "how propaganda works" explainers)
prompt_elements: flat red, black and ochre poster colours
